analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds one row at head line 1751 to the daemon-environment passthrough table, and docs/provider/direct-mode.md describes load-time shape warmup for standalone preload. No executable code, protocol messages, keys, attestation, authorization, cache crypto, or trust-boundary logic is touched. The new DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP row (`0` disables the warmup, `always` skips the shader-cache probe) is a performance-calibration tunable. Per the doc it is listed among variables copied from the invoking shell into the LaunchAgent plist. It does not touch attestation, serving authorization (TB-011/T-053), encrypted prefix-cache gating (T-041), or prompt confidentiality (A-001). Its `always` and `0` values change only warmup behavior, not the security gates.

One point for later review: the cli-reference.md prose before the table says only listed variables are passed through. The new row follows that pattern, so the docs are internally consistent. The truth of the passthrough claim depends on LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys/inferencePassthroughEnvKeys, which was not supplied. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a demonstrated regression. Warmup runs synthetic shapes, so no consumer plaintext is involved, as far as the docs state. The direct-mode.md warmup description (idle-tick warming, preemption by requests) is documentation only, and the actual implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift and the sweep tick was not supplied. No findings. The threat model needs no update.
